thread:
sana: FYI — since the RBAC tweak to the cert-rotator role (yesterday evening) we've seen intermittent TLS handshakes failing for svc-search in eu-west-1. No obvious KMS audit entries for decrypt failures, gap in observability.

ops-bot: ALERT: svc-search TLS handshake error spike (eu-west-1). 120 errors in last 10m. Incident: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-4321 :warning:

alex: can you paste a sample client/server log and any s_client output?

sana: sample from proxy logs — short: "error=handshake failed; reason=bad_certificate; peer=svc-search-3"

sana: openssl s_client -connect svc-search.eu-west-1.internal:443 -showcerts output: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Let's Encrypt, CN = ISRG Root X1
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
---
```

jack: that looks like the cert chain isn't being assembled by the rotator when the secret is mounted. Did the rotator pod lose permission to call KMS:Decrypt for the envelope key?

security-bot: quick checks: 1) query cloudtrail for kms:Decrypt events for the key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 2) check the cert-rotator serviceaccount IAM role binding and the KMS key policy for Allow principals. Example CloudTrail query snippet: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --region eu-west-1 --start-time 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z```

alex: ran the CloudTrail query — got Decrypt events from the rotator 2h before the RBAC change, then nothing during the failure window. Instead there are a handful of "AccessDenied" events but not on the KMS key resource. Looks like the rotator service account got swapped to a different IAM role that doesn't have kms:Decrypt.

oncall-eu: I rolled the RBAC rollback two hours ago back to the previous role binding; rotator is back to old SA. But errors continued for ~30m after. Could be cached secrets on nodes or a rolling deploy didn't reach all pods.

jack: action plan: 1) capture tcpdump on one failing node to see ClientHello SNI and TLS record (tcpdump -w /tmp/tls.pcap port 443 and filter by pod ip). 2) kubectl describe secret cert-search -n prod to confirm secret data and annotations. 3) check aws kms get-key-rotation-status and key policy for the key. 4) rotate a test cert manually and restart rotator to force re-decrypt.

sana: kubectl describe secret output shows annotation: "kmsKeyId=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01" and workload identity mount present. However the cert object in the secret is empty for one pod (looks like failed write).

alex: quick remediation command to patch RoleBinding if needed: ```kubectl patch rolebinding cert-rotator-binding -n infra --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/subjects/0/name","value":"cert-rotator-sa"}]'``` also ensure the IAM role has policy: ```{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
    "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01"]
  }]
}```

security-bot: note for postmortem: add an audit alert for "kms:Decrypt" AccessDenied events where principal matches cert-rotator role. Also track last successful Decrypt timestamp per region and emit a heartbeat metric.

oncall-eu: I collected tcpdump and it shows ClientHello with SNI correct. The server responded with an empty chain for the handshake in the failing case — points to missing cert material on the host.

jack: likely sequence: RBAC change -> rotator lost decrypt perms -> rotator failed to write secret -> some pods restarted and pulled empty cert -> TLS handshake fails until secret repaired or pod restarted. We should: (a) reconcile KMS policies, (b) add a liveness check to cert consumer pods to fail fast if cert missing (force restart and re-fetch), (c) add a rotator self-check that logs decrypt errors to centralized audit with correlation-id.

sana: I'm opening a follow-up ticket with steps to update KMS key policy and RBAC playbook, plus a retro to add the audit alert. Will include the tcpdump and kube outputs.

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1873: "cert rotator kms-decrypt gap / observability alerting" assigned to @jack, @sana. Link: https://redwood.kanban/INFRA-1873 :white_check_mark:

jack: I'll take INFRA-1873. Quick wins: patch key policy to explicitly Allow the cert-rotator role, add CloudTrail metric filter for kms:Decrypt AccessDenied, and add a Grafana panel for last_decrypt_success_timestamp per region.

sana: thanks all — will coordinate the rollback/patch and keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
